picked.t: US rejects record 1 in 4 South Korean visitor visa applicants, over four times Japan's rate
picked.body: The adjusted refusal rate for South Koreans applying for B1 business and B2 tourist visas reached 24.73% in U.S. fiscal year 2025, up 9.76 percentage points from 14.97% a year earlier, according to South Korean Foreign Ministry data released on Oct. 26 by Rep. Kim Dai-sik of the main opposition People Power Party. The figure matches the State Department's published table for fiscal 2025. It is also the highest for South Korea in the department's tables going back to fiscal 2006; the previous peak was 21.2% in fiscal 2014. The adjusted rate leaves out applicants who were refused but later issued a visa in the same year, for example after submitting additional documents. South Korea's rate had ranged from 14.44% to 18.03% in fiscal 2021 through 2024, after 8.46% in 2020. The figures exclude South Koreans who travel under the U.S. Visa Waiver Program, which lets them visit for up to 90 days without a visa once approved through the Electronic System for Travel Authorization (ESTA). The number of B visas issued to South Koreans fell 21.2% to 12,226 from 15,508 a year earlier, The Korea Herald reported. South Korea's rate was more than four times Japan's, which slipped to 5.68% from 5.76%, according to State Department figures. It also exceeded the rates for fellow program members the U.K., at 20.44%, Germany, at 12.22%, and France, at 9.67%, though Ireland's was higher at 25.12%. Rates for China fell to 20.21% from 25.37%, and Vietnam 22.08%, nearly unchanged from 22.12% a year earlier. The Foreign Ministry told Kim's office that Washington does not disclose why visas are refused, making the exact cause difficult to determine. "We presume that tighter visa screening policies may have had an impact as immigration has become an increasingly contentious domestic political issue in the United States," the ministry said, according to Korea JoongAng Daily . Posts from applicants refused at B1 and B2 visa interviews appear regularly on South Korean online communities for U.S. travel and study abroad, with many complaining they were not told why, the Seoul Economic Daily reported. Some observers suggest immigration authorities under President Donald Trump may have classified South Korea as a country of heightened scrutiny, the newspaper said. On Sept. 4, 2025, U.S. immigration agents detained more than 300 South Korean workers at the construction site of a Hyundai Motor and LG Energy Solution battery plant in Georgia. Kim Dai-sik questioned whether relations with Washington also played a role. "We need to closely examine whether our government’s diplomatic and defense policies toward the U.S., as well as changes in Korea-U.S. relations, have contributed to U.S. visa refusals," he said, according to The Korea Herald . Rep. Jung Chung-rae of the ruling Democratic Party, a former party leader, moved from the Foreign Affairs and Unification Committee's Americas audit team to its Europe team on Oct. 8 after his U.S. visa was not issued in time. Democratic Party leader Kim Min-seok also postponed a planned October trip to the U.S. after meetings with members of Congress proved hard to schedule ahead of the midterm elections, the Seoul Economic Daily reported. People Power Party Rep. Na Kyung-won wrote on Facebook on Oct. 15 that the trip had fallen through. She listed the hold on Jung's visa and the cutoff of U.S. intelligence among the problems in relations with Washington, and urged President Lee Jae Myung and his party to first consider ways to normalize the alliance.

picked.t: Vietnamese students top South Korea's visa overstayers with over 26,200 cases
picked.body: The latest data from South Korea's Ministry of Justice showed that the number of international students who remained in the country after their D-2 visas, which cover college, undergraduate and postgraduate studies, expired reached a record high of more than 9,900 as of August. Vietnamese students accounted for the largest share, with more than 6,800 cases, or over 68% of the total, nearly five times the figure for Uzbekistan, which ranked second at more than 14% with 1,412 people. They are followed by Mongolia (738 people, 7.4%), Nepal (318 people, 3.2%), and China (236 people, 2.4%), The Chosun Daily reported. Vietnamese nationals also topped the list of overstayers among students enrolled in Korean language programs under D-4-1 and D-4-7 visas, with more than 19,400 cases, accounting for 89.4% of the total, By nationality, around 40% of Vietnamese students in these programs were found to have violated visa regulations, the second-highest rate after Uzbekistan. The rate was nearly six percentage points higher than a year earlier. By region, Gyeonggi, Gangwon, South Chungcheong and North Chungcheong provinces recorded the highest numbers of international students overstaying their visas. Depending on the circumstances, visa overstayers face fines, imprisonment, deportation and bans on re-entering South Korea. People Power Party Rep. Kim Hee-jung accused universities of focusing on recruiting international students without putting adequate measures in place to ensure they remain enrolled and maintain legal residency status. "Universities, which should be centers of learning, have become backdoor channels for illegal residency," Kim said, as quoted by The Korea Herald . She urged the Education Ministry and Justice Ministry to review the entire international student system, including visa screening, admissions, residency monitoring and post-admission oversight. South Korea has more international students than ever before. The country aimed to attract 300,000 foreign students by 2027 but reached that target in the summer of 2025. The number of international students had risen to 367,700 as of September, according to the Ministry of Justice's Korea Immigration Service. Vietnamese students make up the largest international student group in the country, numbering more than 129,200, or 35% of the total, increasing by over 20,000 from a year earlier. Chinese students ranked second, with more than 89,000, according to University News Network. A study by Kim Gyu-chan, an associate professor at Gangneung-Wonju National University, found that international students overstay their visas or work without authorization largely because of strict employment and visa regulations, financial pressures, and insufficient support for transitioning from education to employment, The Korea Times reported in January. The study also criticized a university accreditation system that uses illegal-stay rates as a key measure, arguing that it could encourage institutions to prioritize immigration monitoring over education and career support. "International students should not simply be viewed as temporary substitutes for the declining school-age population or as administrative burdens," Kim said, as quoted by The Korea Times . "They must be recognized as future residents and valuable human resources." Kim argued that South Korea should regard international students as potential long-term residents and skilled workers rather than temporary labor or administrative burdens. He recommended establishing a unified government data platform, dedicated career support centers and incentives for universities that build partnerships with local businesses.

picked.t: South Korea's top-ranked university eyes students in Vietnam, China for its first international-only division
picked.body: The proposal was discussed at a university senate meeting on Oct. 22, the Korea JoongAng Daily reported. The senate approved setting up the division of global talent in April, and the latest meeting focused on how it will operate. Leading schools in those markets were also named as priority targets, among them the United Nations International School of Hanoi, Taipei Municipal Chien Kuo High School, Taipei First Girls High School and the High School Attached to Northeast Normal University in China. "We are not simply prioritizing countries that have produced large numbers of successful applicants," said Cha Suk-won, SNU's vice president for global affairs. "We are focusing on places with well-established systems for nurturing talent, such as gifted schools and international schools, where a high proportion of applicants are academically outstanding." Faculty and staff from SNU's University College, which will house the division, are scheduled to visit Vietnam in January 2027 to present admissions guidelines to prospective applicants. Visits to Kazakhstan and other countries are under consideration. Vietnamese students became the largest group of international students in South Korea this year, numbering 96,834, or 31.5% of the 307,464 total as of April 1, ahead of 78,890 Chinese students, according to Education Ministry data released in August. SNU is also developing a "fly-in program" that would bring outstanding overseas high school students and prospective incoming students to campus, designed as a targeted recruitment tool rather than a one-off campus visit. Under the proposal, incoming students will be required to take Korean-language courses suited to their Test of Proficiency in Korean (TOPIK) scores before choosing between a humanities, social sciences and arts track and a science and engineering track. They can then pursue at least one major offered by departments across 10 of SNU's undergraduate colleges. The division is expected to admit about 36 students a year outside the regular enrollment quota, leaving the number of places for Korean students unchanged, The Korea Herald reported in April. It is scheduled to be established in March 2027, with classes starting in September. Applicants and both their parents must be foreign nationals, according to SNU's admissions office. SNU, South Korea's highest-ranked university, placed 38th in the 2027 QS World University Rankings released in June, the same as a year earlier but down from 29th in the 2023 edition. Weaker scores for international student ratio and diversity were cited as key factors in the decline. The university has been less aggressive than its peers in recruiting international students. Official data showed it had 1,383 foreign students as of 2025, against 4,740 at Yonsei University and 4,471 at Korea University. As details of the division have emerged, calls have grown within SNU for more consultation with existing undergraduates, the JoongAng Daily reported. Concerns remain that the program could strain educational resources and student welfare services such as classrooms, dormitories and scholarships. Students in programs housed in the same college as the new division have voiced concern that resources and support for them could shrink. "We intend to consult with the university administration to establish a process for gathering feedback from existing members of the university community, particularly students, before the new division begins full operations," a source from SNU's council of college student representatives said.

picked.t: Thailand targets Vietnam, Singapore in Southeast Asia tourism push
picked.body: TAT aims to increase arrivals from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations by 4.3% in the financial year. Apart from Vietnam, the other priority markets are Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore and Taiwan (China). The strategy, outlined in a Commerce Ministry statement on Oct. 23, follows a policy set by Deputy Prime Minister and Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun to bring together the commerce, culture, and tourism and sports ministries. Suphajee’s policy aims to turn Thailand’s hosting of the 2026 Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank into lasting economic benefits by connecting tourism, Thai products and cultural influence, or soft power, The Nation reported. The initiative linking tourism, trade and culture aims to expand market opportunities, increase the value of goods and services, and distribute income to businesses and local communities. TAT will focus on families and shopping in Vietnam, while its Malaysian campaign will emphasize food, shopping and travel to secondary cities. For Indonesia, TAT will promote wellness and Muslim-friendly tourism. In Singapore, the authority will target visitors with strong spending power and an interest in quality travel experiences. TAT’s Taiwan strategy centers on Thai food and culinary tourism, alongside the "Go Thai Be Free" campaign presenting Thailand as an open and welcoming destination for LGBTQ+ travelers. TAT has presented seven tourism routes in Bangkok and 20 travel programs through the Association of Thai Travel Agents (ATTA) to encourage meeting participants to extend their stays and spend more in Thailand.

picked.t: The journey through unexplored jungle to discover 2-ha sinkhole in Phong Nha - Ke Bang
picked.body: In 2023, while searching on Google Earth, Nguyen Van Uy, deputy director of Jungle Boss Tours and a member of the U.S.-based National Speleological Society (NSS), discovered the black spot in the forest in the Cha Noi - Khe Gat area, within the core zone of the national park. The low resolution of the image made it impossible for him to decide if it was a sinkhole. He tried to fly a drone to inspect the area, but it could only reach a maximum altitude of 500 meters and not clear a mountain in its path. Later that year, Kevin Ditamore, a member of the NSS, visited Phong Nha - Ke Bang and met with Uy. They were surprised to find that they had both noticed the same black spot, and suspected it to be a sinkhole or a cave entrance. After cross-checking, they confirmed the two locations were the same. Ditamore returned home, leaving further exploration on hold. In early 2025, with a drone capable of flying up to 1,000 meters, Uy and some American experts surveyed the terrain three times. Uy says: "The aerial images recorded the mouth of the hole right in the middle of the primary forest. I confirmed that it was a sinkhole." By April 2025, a 10-member team, including two forest rangers, set off from Da Dao pass on the Ho Chi Minh highway in Phong Nha Commune, Quang Tri Province. Carrying over 35 kg of gear each, they trekked into the jungle to locate a way to the sinkhole's mouth. The sinkhole lies deep within the primary forest in hazardous terrain with no established trails. Even the National Park rangers and experienced trekkers were unaware of a route leading there. Team members had to push their way through dense vegetation, branches, and sharp thorns that sliced through skin and drew blood. Jungle leeches clung to their legs, staining their protective socks with blood. Near-vertical cliffs forced the expedition members to cling to tree trunks, treading cautiously step-by-step to prevent slipping and falling. At the end of each day, the team pitched tents, prepared meals, and rested overnight. Meals consisted mostly of dry rations, and the members had to replenish its limited water supply from forest streams. However, with the area being dominated by limestone mountains, there are very few streams, leaving them with no choice but to endure severe thirst at times. Two days passed, but the opening of the sinkhole was nowhere to be found. The team often had to change direction on encountering rock faces or impassable brush. The rugged, uneven trail and dense tangles of vines made trekking extremely difficult and gradually sapped the team's strength. By the end of the third day, as the group split into three directions to search, one member suddenly spotted the sinkhole's opening beneath the forest canopy. It was far larger than what had appeared in the drone footage. Uy says: "Everyone burst into tears of joy. We were all panting heavily after scaling the steep slopes, but the excitement felt like discovering buried treasure. Despite being hungry and parched, nobody cared, everyone just rushed over to get a look at the sinkhole's opening." Lacking the necessary gear to descend to the bottom and with rations sufficient for only a five-day itinerary, the team decided to record the coordinates, return, and prepare for a major expedition. "All 10 members were experienced trekkers with mountain-climbing skills, but upon returning home, every single one of us was left with scars from being cut by the jungle vegetation," Uy says. Building on the findings from April 2025, a full-scale survey was launched from July 23 to 29. The 24-member expedition team included NSS experts, the Jungle Boss technical crew, forest rangers, and Ditamore. The expedition team carried 500 meters of specialized rope, protective gear, and food supplies, with each person carrying a 30-kg load. After trekking over 20 km through the jungle, navigating sharp cat's-claw limestone rocks and sheer vertical slopes, the members reached the sinkhole's mouth, pitched camp, and divided into two groups. One team rigged the ropes for the experts to rappel down and survey, while the other took care of logistical support. Every day, six experts took turns rappelling down into the sinkhole to examine the terrain, rock faces, and geological features. The remaining members cooked the meals, transported water, and managed the other logistical operations. The survey found the sinkhole spread over an area of 2.1 hectares in Compartment 8, Sub-zone 603, a strictly protected zone of the Phong Nha - Ke Bang National Park. It has an oval-shaped opening measuring about 190 meters long and 140 meters wide. Inside, the maximum length reaches 250 meters, with a width of 200 meters and a depth of 120 meters. A notable feature is that the rock walls expand outward from top to bottom like an inverted bowl. The interior of the sinkhole is wider than its mouth, forming a massive chamber. picked.t: BigBang members share backstage photos, show love for Vietnamese fans after Hanoi concerts
picked.body: After the second show ended on Oct. 25, Taeyang uploaded a collection of photos to his official Facebook page, attracting more than 12,000 likes, comments and shares within an hour. Fans flooded the comments with well-wishes, while some expressed disappointment that he had not performed his hit song "Eyes, Nose, Lips". Across both nights, Taeyang entertained the audience with energetic and technically demanding dance routines. While performing "Bad", he executed a trust fall into the arms of his backup dancers. During "Live Fast Die Slow", he approached the crowd barrier and passed his microphone to fans, inviting them to sing along. On the second night, he emerged victorious in a dance competition against his two bandmates. Daesung also marked the occasion on Instagram, sharing photos of himself holding two handheld banners prepared by G-Dragon's Vietnamese fan community. The banners carried the messages "BigBang is back" and "Until Whenever, Still BigBang Still V.I.P.", referring to the group's official fandom name. Known for his sense of humor, Daesung repeatedly amused the audience during the shows. He revealed that he had struggled to sleep after the opening night because he kept recalling the memorable moments he had shared with fans. At both concerts, he performed the Vietnamese phrase "Qua gioi han, qua gioi han" (Beyond limits, beyond limits), an adapted lyric from his song "Hando-Chogu", while swaying his hips, prompting loud cheers. Although G-Dragon has yet to publish a post about the concerts, the group's leader remained active online, liking Daesung's update and several videos showing Vietnamese fans singing along. The Oct. 24–25 performances were part of BigBang's 2026–2027 world tour, "XX: COSMOS", celebrating 20 years since the group's debut. The setlists were largely identical across both nights, featuring fan favorites including "Fantastic Baby", "Hands Up", "Blue", "Tonight" and "Lies". At the end of the first show, the three members knelt to express their gratitude to the audience and described the event at My Dinh National Stadium as "the best concert." Following the second performance, Daesung jokingly suggested signing a contract for another concert in Vietnam, a proposal warmly welcomed by Taeyang and G-Dragon. All three pledged to return to the country soon. During the Oct. 24 show, G-Dragon had also told the audience: "This is just the beginning." BigBang debuted in 2006 with five members: G-Dragon, Taeyang, T.O.P, Seungri and Daesung. The group gained recognition for its hip-hop and R&B-influenced sound, powerful vocals, synchronized performances and songwriting skills. It collected numerous Artist of the Year, Song of the Year and Album of the Year honors at major Asian music awards, expanding its popularity to the U.S. by 2010. In 2015, the group released its third Korean-language studio album, "MADE", which enjoyed widespread success. Its activities slowed in 2018 as the members began their mandatory military service, with "Flower Road" becoming the last single featuring all five original members. When BigBang returned in 2022, it had four members, following Seungri's departure after he received a three-year prison sentence in August 2021. T.O.P subsequently left the group two years later. In 2024, BigBang attracted renewed attention with a three-member performance at the Mnet Asian Music Awards. The group first visited Vietnam in 2012, when all five original members performed at the SoundFest music festival in Ho Chi Minh.

picked.t: Vietnam, Poland establish strategic partnership, set $6B trade target
picked.body: Prime Minister Le Minh Hung and his Polish counterpart Donald Tusk announced the outcome of their talks at a press conference. The two sides adopted a joint statement establishing the partnership and an action plan to strengthen ties for 2026-2030, the Vietnam News Agency reported. They pledged close coordination on implementing the EU-Vietnam Free Trade Agreement (EVFTA) effectively as they work toward the $6 billion target, up from $3.95 billion in 2025. The leaders also agreed to make greater use of the ASEAN-EU strategic partnership to help strengthen each country's strategic autonomy, secure supply chains, ensure energy and food security, and respond to climate change. The two sides agreed that Poland would serve as a gateway for Vietnamese goods into Central and Eastern European markets. They will also work to make Vietnam a key gateway, destination and platform for Polish and other EU businesses seeking to reach the ASEAN market. The prime ministers agreed to promote cooperation in energy transition, smart agriculture, digital transformation, space technology and pharmaceuticals, tying it to technology transfer and sustainable development. Cooperation will also cover strategic infrastructure projects in railways, shipbuilding and transport, as well as the green transition and the environment. PM Hung said the two sides agreed to further deepen defense and security cooperation and to pursue substantive cooperation in fighting transnational and high-tech crime, cybersecurity and non-traditional security. They also agreed to make science and technology, innovation and digital transformation a new pillar of the strategic partnership. They will strengthen the Vietnam-Poland joint committee on science and technology cooperation to identify priority programs and projects with concrete results. Vietnam and Poland will also step up cooperation in training, scientific research and technology transfer among their universities, research institutes and businesses. The leaders agreed to increase scholarships and strengthen cooperation in cultural industries, film and performing arts, the restoration of historical relics, and sports, including exchanges between the two countries' Olympic committees.

picked.t: 베트남항공, 다낭-싱가포르 신규 취항…내달 17일 첫 운항
picked.body: (사진=베트남항공) 국영 베트남항공(Vietnam Airlines)이 내달부터 다낭과 싱가포르를 잇는 노선을 신규 취항한다. 이로써 베트남항공의 싱가포르 국제선 노선은 주 42회로 늘어나게 된다. 베트남항공에 따르면, 오는 11월 17일부터 다낭-싱가포르 직항편이 매일 운항될 예정이다. 해당 노선에는 A321기가 투입되며, 다낭발 항공편은 15시(현지시간), 복편은 19시 45분에 출발한다. 현재 베트남항공은 △하노이-싱가포르 주 14회 △호치민시-싱가포르 주 21회 노선을 운항하고 있다. 이에 따라 다낭-싱가포르 주 7회 노선이 추가되면 동사가 운항 중인 싱가포르 노선은 주당 42회로 늘어난다. 베트남항공은 “싱가포르는 베트남을 찾는 주요 관광 시장 중 하나”라고 이번 신규 취항의 배경을 설명했다. 실제로 9월 기준 베트남을 찾은 외국인 관광객 가운데, 싱가포르 출신 관광객은 전년 동기 대비 29.8% 증가했는데, 특히 다낭은 싱가포르 여행객들이 자주 찾는 여행지 중 하나다. 올 들어 베트남항공은 암스테르담, 콜롬보, 푸켓 등 국제선에 잇따라 취항하며 국제선 운항망을 확대하고 있다. 이 밖에도 베트남항공은 오는 11월 3일 하노이-아메다바드, 11월 22일 하노이-항저우 노선 신규 취항을 앞두고 있다.
